title: Pinecone Developer
description: Manage Pinecone indexes and upsert, search, and rerank records (integrated inference), plus search the Pinecone docs, via the official Pinecone Developer MCP server.

env_vars.name: PINECONE_API_KEY
env_vars.description: Pinecone API key from the console (app.pinecone.io). Required to list/create/upsert/query indexes; without it only docs search works. Pass via env, never inline in args (doctrine #6).

auth.recipe: generate an API key in the Pinecone console (app.pinecone.io) and set PINECONE_API_KEY.

sample_tools.name: describe-index
sample_tools.summary: Describe the configuration of an index.

sample_tools.name: describe-index-stats
sample_tools.summary: Get statistics about an index, including record count and namespaces.

sample_tools.name: create-index-for-model
sample_tools.summary: Create a new index that uses an integrated inference model to embed text.

sample_tools.name: upsert-records
sample_tools.summary: Insert or update records in an index with integrated inference.

sample_tools.name: search-records
sample_tools.summary: Search records in an index by text query, with metadata filtering and reranking.

sample_tools.name: rerank-documents
sample_tools.summary: Rerank a collection of records or text documents with a reranking model.

known_limitations: Requires a PINECONE_API_KEY for index management and queries; without a key the server can still search Pinecone documentation but cannot list, create, upsert, or search your indexes.

Only Pinecone indexes with integrated inference are supported — assistants, indexes without integrated inference, standalone embeddings, and standalone vector search are not exposed; create a compatible index with create-index-for-model.
Runs via `npx -y @pinecone-database/mcp` and needs Node.js v18+ with npx on PATH; it reaches the Pinecone control/data plane at api.pinecone.io, so outbound network access is required.
Destructive-action audit (X2.18): no destructive tools — the tools list/describe/search/upsert/rerank records and create indexes; none delete indexes or records, so destructive_tools is empty.

client_install.claude_desktop: Add to claude_desktop_config.json mcpServers as `pinecone`: { command: npx, args: [-y, @pinecone-database/mcp], env: { PINECONE_API_KEY: "..." } }.
client_install.cursor: Create .cursor/mcp.json with server `pinecone` running `npx -y @pinecone-database/mcp`; set PINECONE_API_KEY in the env. Also installable as a Gemini CLI extension from github.com/pinecone-io/pinecone-mcp.
client_install.vscode: Add to .vscode/mcp.json servers as `pinecone` with command `npx -y @pinecone-database/mcp`; supply PINECONE_API_KEY via inputs.
